events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Light snow expected. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 30 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Lycoming, Potter, Sullivan, and Tioga Counties.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Be prepared for winter driving conditions overnight
through the Friday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall will be elevation-dependent with
accumulation most likely above 1500 feet. Snow is most likely to
accumulate on non-paved surfaces. The first snow of the season can
result in greater impacts as motorists adjust to winter driving
conditions.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 50 mph expected.

* WHERE...Humboldt County, and Interior Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Wind gusts will be particularly strong along windward
ridges and exposed coastal headlands. Gusty winds will blow around
unsecured objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power
outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be strong aloft and may mix down to
the surface, resulting in wind advisory conditions.

* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Del Norte Coast.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.

especially early to mid morning Friday, due to strong winds aloft
mixing down to the surface. High Winds are especially likely
immediately along the coast north of Crescent City Harbor and
coastal headlands.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.
